subject: FinEdge procurement: request for termination rights and escrow / fee-at-risk
messages:
From: Hilary Tyson <hilary.tyson@finedge.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Derek Collins <derek.collins@finedge.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Apr 2026 13:42:00 -0400
Subject: Redwood SLA and procurement asks

Rafael — thanks again for the demo last week. FinEdge is eager to move forward but procurement and legal have a couple of non-negotiable asks before we can sign: they need either (A) explicit termination rights for repeated SLA breaches plus a fee-at-risk held in escrow, or (B) liquidated damages capped at three months of fees for severe outages.

To be concrete: our procurement team is asking for the ability to terminate for cause if Redwood misses the committed uptime/latency SLOs in three separate months inside any rolling 12-month period, after a 30-day cure period. They also want an escrow equal to two months of monthly committed fees that would be released to FinEdge in the event of validated breaches.

FinEdge is in a regulated vertical and these protections are standard for us. We recognize this is not typical for SaaS; if Redwood cannot accept either A or B, please let me know quickly so we can evaluate alternatives. Attaching our RFP schedule and the procurement team's markup.

Hilary
Head of Procurement, FinEdge

Attachment: FinEdge_RFP-schedule.pdf (stub)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Hilary Tyson <hilary.tyson@finedge.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Apr 2026 15:10:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Redwood SLA and procurement asks

Hilary — really appreciate the clarity and the specifics. I hear you that FinEdge needs strong contractual protections given regulatory risk. Two quick things: 1) we generally offer credits for SLA misses rather than liquidated damages, and 2) termination-for-cause on short SLA counts is a material risk for our platform customers.

That said, we want this to work. I’m looping in Neha from Legal and Marissa (my manager) so we can review procurement's markup and propose a path that balances your needs with platform risk. Typical alternatives we've offered to other regulated customers include: an escrowed fee-at-risk limited to a small multiple of monthly committed fees, a defined major-incident trigger (not just month-level percentage) for termination rights, and a robust cure period/operational remediation plan.

Can we schedule a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk legal through a proposed counter? If you prefer, we can send a redline first.

Thanks — Rafael
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Attachment: SLA_draft_v2.pdf (stub)

From: Hilary Tyson <hilary.tyson@finedge.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Redwood SLA and procurement asks

Rafael — thanks. Procurement will only accept contractual remedies that provide a credible path to remediation for us — credits are not sufficient because they don't address replacement costs and regulatory risk. A few clarifying points from our side:

- The request for three separate months is a floor, not a ceiling; procurement expects termination may be triggered earlier for severe incidents that cause material customer/market impact.
- The escrow must be accessible within 30 days of a validated breach decision (we can accept an arbiter clause).
- If you propose an incident-based definition for termination, we need sample language and examples of what qualifies as a "severe" incident.

If legal can send redlines today, we can review before a call.

Hilary

Subject: Fwd: Redwood SLA and procurement asks — FinEdge wants escrow/termination rights (internal)

Team — forwarding FinEdge procurement asks. High level: they insist on either termination rights tied to SLA misses + escrow/fee-at-risk OR liquidated damages capped at 3 months.

Quick internal notes (do not forward verbatim to customer):
- Risk: Accepting unilateral termination for month-level SLO misses is precedent-setting and could expose us to churn and workload instability across multi-tenant pools.
- Legal options: 1) Offer incident-triggered termination for cause (e.g., 3 "major" incidents in 90 days with documented customer impact and failure to remedy after 30 days); 2) Offer escrow/fee-at-risk but capped (max 2 months) and only payable after independent validation; 3) Replace liquidated damages with a blended remedy: immediate invoice credits + capped escrow payout for validated severe outages.
- Commercial ask: try to keep fee-at-risk escrow <= 2 months of committed fees and include a mandatory operational remediation plan (ops review, weekly sync, root-cause and a fixes timeline).

I'll draft a redline for SLA and proposed language for incident definition. Thoughts?

—Rafael

On Tue, Apr 21, 2026 at 9:12 AM Hilary Tyson <hilary.tyson@finedge.com> wrote:
> Rafael — thanks. Procurement will only accept contractual remedies...

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Hilary Tyson <hilary.tyson@finedge.com>
Cc: Derek Collins <derek.collins@finedge.com>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2026 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood SLA and procurement asks

Hi Hilary — thank you for the prompt feedback and for sharing procurement's constraints. We want to be cooperative and propose the following as a balanced, executable solution: 

1) Termination-for-cause: permitted only if Redwood experiences three validated "Major Incidents" within a rolling 90-day window OR a single "Catastrophic Incident" as defined below. Major Incident = service outage impacting production traffic resulting in either (a) >10% of tokens failing to be served within SLO for >2 hours, or (b) a sustained regional outage impacting >30% of your traffic for >30 minutes. Catastrophic Incident = complete loss of service for more than 4 hours across your primary region.

2) Cure and operational remediation: any validated incident that could trigger termination provides Redwood a 30-day cure/remediation period with weekly remediation checkpoints. Termination may proceed only if remediation fails to materially address root causes and customer impact.

3) Fee-at-risk / escrow: Redwood will agree to a capped escrow equal to 2 months of committed fees. Escrow release requires independent validation (agreed third-party arbiter) and will be disbursed within 45 days of validation. This replaces a liquidated damages clause; we will not agree to open-ended LDs.

4) Fallback credits: for typical SLA misses we will continue to offer our standard credits ladder (detailed in the attached redline). For verified Major Incidents, we will provide enhanced credits plus the escrow remedy above.

5) DocuSign + redline: I attached a redline to the SLA (SLA_draft_v2.pdf) that includes the incident definitions and escrow mechanics. If this structure is acceptable to procurement, we can send the DocuSign envelope and have Legal finalize the arbiter details.

Proposed next step: 30-minute legal-to-legal call tomorrow at 10am ET to finalize the arbiter and escrow mechanics. Please confirm availability.

Thanks — Rafael
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Attachment: SLA_draft_v2.pdf (redline included)
